extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of ancient Athens / readers of classical political institutions
extracted.subtask_description: A descriptive account of the offices, selection methods, duties, procedural rules, and sanctions in classical Athenian civic and legal institutions. Covers election/lot procedures, specific magistracies, jury selection and conduct, and penalties/rewards for officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cavalry enrollment and inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: Roll of the cavalry is drawn up by the Commissioners of Enrolment (Catalogeis) and handed to Hipparchs and Phylarchs; sworn affidavits and Council vote determine suitability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those who cannot keep up or will not stand steady are branded and disqualified; those claiming incapacity (physical or pecuniary) may be struck out or dismissed; if no affidavit, Council votes whether individual is suitable and enters name on tablet if affirmative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council supervision of public building plans (historical note)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formerly the Council decided plans for public buildings and contracts (e.g., robe of Athena), but this function was transferred to a jury in the law-courts because of perceived favouritism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates principle that decisions subject to popular/randomized review when favouritism suspected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council role in manufacture supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council shares with the Military Treasurer the superintendence of manufacture of images of Victory and Panathenaic prizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council involvement in festival prize production and oversight with treasurers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for infirm paupers
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons possessing less than three minas and so crippled as to be unable to work, after examination by the Council, are to receive two obols a day from the state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A treasurer is appointed by lot to attend to them; establishes means-tested public relief administered after council examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioners for Repairs of Temples
rubrics_metrics.description: Ten Commissioners for Repairs of Temples elected by lot receive thirty minas from the Receivers-General to carry out necessary temple repairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies number, selection by lot, and fixed appropriation for duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: City Commissioners (Astynomi) duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Ten City Commissioners (five for Piraeus, five for the city) oversee hiring of female musicians at not more than two drachmas, resolve competing hirings by lot, regulate sewage disposal, prevent street-blocking constructions, and remove corpses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They have a body of state slaves assigned for corpse removal; specific local-regulatory and public-health remit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market Commissioners (Agoranomi) duty
rubrics_metrics.description: Five for Piraeus and five for the city are elected by lot; their statutory duty is to see that all articles offered for sale in the market are pure and unadulterated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consumer protection by market oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioners of Weights and Measures (Metronomi)
rubrics_metrics.description: Five for the city and five for Piraeus, elected by lot, to ensure sellers use fair weights and measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforces measurement standards in commerce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corn Commissioners (Sitophylaces) duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Originally ten (now increased) elected by lot; duties include ensuring unprepared corn sold at reasonable prices, millers sell barley meal at a proportionate price to barley, bakers sell loaves at prices proportionate to wheat and of such weight as Commissioners appoint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Law requires them to fix standard loaf weight; explicit price-and-weight regulation to prevent market abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Superintendents of the Mart
rubrics_metrics.description: Ten superintendents elected by lot to superintend the Mart and compel merchants to bring two-thirds of the corn brought by sea into the city Corn Mart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Market supply regulation to ensure sufficient city provisioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Eleven: prison management and prosecutions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Eleven, appointed by lot, take care of prisoners in the state gaol; thieves/kidnappers/pickpockets who plead guilty are executed; those denying charges are brought before law-courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They also bring state-property claims and informations against magistrates; coordinate with Commissioners for Public Contracts when property deemed state-owned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introducers of Cases (Eisagogeis) and 'monthly' cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Five Introducers of Cases (one per pair of tribes) elected by lot bring 'monthly' cases to law-courts (e.g., refusal to pay dowry, interest disputes, slander, loans, partnership disputes, slave/cattle/trierarch/bank issues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cases ≤ ten drachmas can be decided summarily; larger amounts are brought into the law-courts as 'monthly' cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Forty and small-claims jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: The Forty (four from each tribe) hear suits where amount at issue does not exceed ten drachmas; larger amounts are handed to Arbitrators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically thirty, increased to forty; they formerly went on circuit through demes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arbitrators: procedure and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Arbitrators take cases handed up; if they cannot reconcile parties they give a decision. If appealed, they enclose evidence/pleadings/laws in two urns (plaintiff/defendant) with arbitrator's decision and pass to justices to introduce to law-court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On appeal juries may only consider materials enclosed in the urns (no new evidence); arbitrators are persons in their sixtieth year; arbitrator failing duty loses civil rights (with right of appeal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of arbitrations by lot and compulsory service
rubrics_metrics.description: Arbitrations are assigned by lot among the Eponymi of a year; every one is compelled to carry through arbitrations assigned by lot; failing to serve when of required age causes loss of civil rights unless exempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures distribution and enforcement of arbitration duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioners of Roads (Hodopoei)
rubrics_metrics.description: Five Commissioners of Roads, with public slaves, required to keep the roads in order; elected by lot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple public-works supervisory role with assigned labor force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auditors: account examination and sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Ten Auditors with ten assistants examine accounts of office-holders; can bring them up for examination before law-courts and, if embezzlement is detected, the jury condemn him for theft and he must repay tenfold; bribe convictees are fined for corruption and repay tenfold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unfair dealing fines are single-sum if paid before ninth prytany, else doubled; tenfold fine is not doubled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clerk of the prytany and Clerk of the Laws duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Clerk of the prytany (elected by lot) has charge of public documents, keeps Assembly resolutions, checks transcripts, attends Council; Clerk of the Laws (also by lot) attends Council sessions and checks law transcripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically elected by open vote and usually trustworthy; now by lot; Assembly also elects a reader-clerk by open vote whose only duty is reading documents aloud.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioners of Public Worship and Annual Commissioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioners for Sacrifices (Hieropoei) elected by lot offer sacrifices appointed by oracle and, with seers, take auspices; ten Annual Commissioners (by lot) offer certain sacrifices and administer quadrennial festivals (except Panathenaea).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists quadrennial festivals (Delos, Brauronia, Heracleia, Eleusinia, Panathenaea) and notes additions; selection by lot for sacred duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archon and Demarch local festivals
rubrics_metrics.description: An Archon is elected by lot for Salamis and a Demarch for Piraeus to celebrate the Dionysia and appoint Choregi; in Salamis the Archon's name is publicly recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local religious/festival administrative duties are delegated to these officers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archon selection, examination, and oath
rubrics_metrics.description: Nine Archons (including six Thesmothetae by lot, plus Archon, King, Polemarch) are examined by the Council and the law-court on genealogy, possession of ancestral cults, family tomb, treatment of parents, taxes, and military service; witnesses are called and accusations heard; then they swear an oath on the stone and repeat it on the Acropolis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All magistrates are examined before taking office; former procedures changed to allow appeals to law-courts; oath includes not receiving presents or dedicating a golden statue if they do.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archon duties: festivals, Choregi assignments, and legal referrals
rubrics_metrics.description: Archon issues a proclamation preserving prior possessions, assigns Choregi to tragic poets, receives Choregi appointed by tribes for choruses, transacts property exchanges and excuses, superintends sacred processions and contests, and brings preliminary inquiries for certain suits to law-courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies age requirement for choregus of boys' chorus (>40); state contributes funds for processions; Archon manages particular festivals and contests.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of suits the Archon brings up
rubrics_metrics.description: After preliminary inquiry the Archon brings actions such as injury to parents, injury to orphans, wards of state disputes, mental derangement claims, appointment of liquidators, wardship determinations, inspection of disputed property, grants of guardianship, inheritance and ward disputes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Archon has care of orphans/wards and can fine or litigate guardians who fail duties; leases orphan/ward houses until age fourteen and may take mortgages.

rubrics_metrics.name: King's judicial and religious functions
rubrics_metrics.description: King superintends mysteries with Superintendents of Mysteries, manages Lenaean Dionysia procession and contest, manages torch-race contests, administers ancestral sacrifices, handles indictments for impiety and priestly-rite disputes, and introduces homicide and wounding cases (some tried in Areopagus).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When King hears a case he removes crown; certain homicide categories tried in Areopagus, Palladium, Delphinium, or Phreatto; Ephetae try other cases within sacred precincts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polemarch duties for aliens
rubrics_metrics.description: Polemarch performs certain sacrifices, organizes funeral contests for war dead, and handles private actions concerning resident aliens and foreign agents; divides alien cases into ten groups assigned by lot to tribes for arbitrators' handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acts for aliens in similar ways the Archon does for citizens; personally brings certain alien-related cases (deserting patron, inheritances involving aliens).

rubrics_metrics.name: Thesmothetae duties and lot-casting for courts
rubrics_metrics.description: Thesmothetae prescribe court days, assign courts to magistrates, introduce impeachments to the Assembly, bring votes for removal from office, handle certain indictments requiring deposit, bring magistrate examinations and condemnations, cast lots for jurors with Archons, and ratify commercial treaties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They bring up specific private suits (merchandise, mines) and perjury from the Areopagus; casting of lots for jurors is performed by nine Archons plus clerk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioners of Games (Athlothetae) duties and oil collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Ten Commissioners of Games (one per tribe), after examination and serving four years, manage Panathenaic procession, musical/gymnastic/horse contests, provide robe of Athena and vases with Council, and present oil to athletes collected from sacred olives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Archon requisitions three-quarters of a pint of oil from each sacred olive farm; Treasurers preserve oil until Panathenaea when measured out to Commissioners and victors; lists prize types (silver/gold, shields, oil).

rubrics_metrics.name: Military officers elected by open vote and confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: Officers connected with military service (ten Generals/Strategi, ten Taxiarchs, Hipparchs, Phylarchs, etc.) are elected by open vote; duties assigned by open vote; appointments are submitted for confirmation each prytany and may be tried if rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generals have full powers on active service to arrest, cashier, or fine for insubordination; military offices may be held multiple times unlike most civil offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between lot and open vote elections
rubrics_metrics.description: Many magistrates are elected by lot while military and some others are elected by open vote; some offices formerly apportioned among demes are now elected from whole tribes due to selling of elections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains historical shifts and rationale (preventing purchase of offices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay and allowances for civic service
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the Assembly receive a drachma for ordinary meetings and nine obols for sovereign meetings; jurors receive three obols; Council members five obols; Prytanes an obol for maintenance; nine Archons four obols each and upkeep of a herald and flute-player; Archon for Salamis a drachma a day; other specific allowances for Commissioners and deputies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Military offices get allowances when sent to islands; membership of Council may be held twice; other offices usually once.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury qualification and selection framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Juries chosen by lot by nine Archons (one per tribe) and clerk to Thesmothetae; all persons above thirty qualified provided not state debtors or having lost civil rights; ten entrances, twenty rooms for lot-drawing, hundred chests and ticket system with letter divisions (alpha to kappa).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an unqualified person serves as juror an information is laid; conviction results in fines and imprisonment until payment of debts and fines; juror tickets bear name, father's name, deme, and a letter; Thesmothetae decide letters required to attend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ticket-hanger and ticket/ball/dice lot procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Ticket-hanger (Empectes) chosen by lot from chest-ticket holders hangs up tickets; Archon casts dice (white/black according to ratio) to choose jurors; names called as dice drawn; selected jurors draw counters from vase and place ticket in chest matching counter letter to assign court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed to prevent tampering or assembling desired jurors into one court; ticket-hanger included among those selected; use of colored dice and counters ensures randomness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court assignment via staff colors and vouchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Each juror receives a staff colored to match assigned court and a voucher on entry; staff color and letter prevent juror switching courts; vouchers used to claim pay and to regulate admission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Officials later call jurors by name and pay them in assigned small groups to avoid crowding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of presiding magistrates and court officials by lot
rubrics_metrics.description: Two ballot boxes and sets of brazen dice with court-colours and dice with magistrates' names are used; Thesmothetae (two selected by lot) throw colours into one box and magistrates' names into the other to assign magistrates to courts anonymously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also, presiding magistrate draws ten tickets (one per tribe) and selects five to appoint a water-clock superintendent and four tellers of votes to prevent preselection/tampering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time regulation of speeches using water-clocks
rubrics_metrics.description: Water-clocks with supply-tubes regulate length of pleadings; time allowances depend on amount at issue: >5,000 drachmas = 10 gallons first speech, 3 gallons second; 1–5,000 = 7 and 2; <1,000 = 5 and 2; arbitrations get 6 gallons with no second speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Superintendent places hand on supply tube when clerk reads resolutions; measured day based on Poseideon day-length; measured day used for cases with severe penalties (imprisonment, death, exile, loss of civil rights, confiscation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Court sizes and combined juries
rubrics_metrics.description: Most courts consist of 500 members; for public cases two courts combine (1,000); most important cases use 1,500 jurors (three courts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates scalability of jury size for case importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ballot procedure for voting and vote-count display
rubrics_metrics.description: Ballot balls made of brass with stems—half pierced, half solid. Officials give each juror two balls (one pierced, one solid) in view of litigants; jurors cast chosen ball into a brazen urn (effective votes) and the other into a wooden urn (unused). Brazen urn has lid pierced to admit one ball at a time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Officials take jurors' staves in exchange for a brass voucher (numeral 3) to ensure they vote; after voting attendants empty brazen urn onto a reckoning board with cavities to display and count votes plainly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protests before voting and declaration of ballot meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Before voting the crier asks whether litigants protest against any evidence (no protests after voting begins) and proclaims which ballot (pierced or solid) corresponds to plaintiff or defendant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures last chance for contesting evidence and clarity about vote meanings.
